regions.full_page: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favor of last week. I am sending the certificates, etc., under separate cover. I am glad you told me of the handicapped little girl with the brain tumor. And since you give such details of the parents etc., I hope the whole "tragedy" may turn to have been a blessing in dis- guise; viz, to bring the child and all concerned closer to the dear Lord. I am going to copy some notes I made on a case of brain-tumor, the cure of which I know about. This case came to my know- ledge almost three years ago, when two ladies came to the Monastery Office on Mt. Elliot Ave. in Detroit, Michigan; Feb. 23rd, 1943. The elderly of the two introduced the younger: " ... This is Mrs. Wheeler who is not of our faith but whose husband is very sick and she would like to speak to you about him." Mrs. Wheeler was weeping. I asked her what denomination they belonged to and she answered: "Methodist." "Well, thank the dear Lord," I answered, "we're both Christians, so that in a way you belong to my faith anyhow because after all there is only one Christianity." "But what is the trouble?" "My husband had a tumor removed from his brain just a month ago today and just this morning they performed the third operation on him. They give me very little hope of his recovery ." .... "Now Mrs. Wheeler, I have a proposition for you to make." .... It was Tuesday. "You make a promise to the Good God in your own honest way that if your husband gives the doctors a surprise tomorrow, or by the end of the week, you will be earnest about finding out for your- self, at least something of the difference, or better said, something of the relationship between your denomination as a Methodist and the "Mother Church." "I'll do anything to please the Lord," she said weeping, "if He'll only spare my poor, dear husband."
